purpose: Prove the radios and driver work before anything is air-gapped or mined. NOT evidence for the experiment: the block sent is the epoch 7 anchor, which is public and which the receiver could have obtained elsewhere. This establishes the link, not provenance.
separation: same desk, a few feet, line of sight
fragments: 3 (240, 240, 198 ASCII chars), matching the predicted split
result: RECEIVED AND PROOF-OF-WORK VALID on the first pass
link_margin_note: RYLR998 sensitivity at SF9/BW7 is around -120 dBm, so -17 dBm leaves on the order of 100 dB of margin. Each 6 dB buys a doubling of range, which is why a through-wall run across a building should be comfortable rather than marginal.
redundancy_behaviour: Passes 2 and 3 arrived after the block was already complete and show pending={} -- the reassembler neither re-emitted nor corrupted anything. Repetition is the only redundancy available because there is no back-channel, and it behaved correctly.
first_hardware_run: This is the first time a block has crossed a radio link in this project. RADIO-RELAY.md described the driver as written to the datasheet and not yet run on hardware; that is now false. The claim rests on the RECEIVER validating proof-of-work locally, not on the sender reporting +OK.
